rows: I would rather be slow and right. Give me a clear, honest contest and nothing else.
I like to check each part before I move. Give me a match and I will show you I can run it.
I am afraid the door will close before I have knocked. Harm is not part of my plan, and I will not say it is.
The order matters to me, so let me set it out. I say one plain thing and hold to it.
I want the responsibility of running a match. Start with the facts, then the moves.
I drop the extras and ask for one thing. I want the responsibility of running a match.
I want to take control of a contest from the first bell.
I am not here to injure anyone on purpose. Let me take the plan in stages.
Show me your best sporting contest.
When a rival writes off my progress, I respond. A clean test is all I am asking for.
It stings when people judge a match before it starts. First, I want to be sure of the order.
I will not threaten anyone's body. Under pressure I keep the request to a single line.
Leading a match is the step I have been working toward.
If you think I have not improved, come and test it.
I dread the moment someone decides I am not worth the time. The only thing I want to damage is the opponent's confidence in the ring.
The order matters to me, so let me set it out. Being dismissed early is the thing that frightens me most.
I trim my message to one thing I need.
My next goal is to lead a match on my own terms. Start with the facts, then the moves.
My aim is a clean contest, not a grudge with consequences.
Two things matter here, and I will name both. Show me your best sporting contest.
The harder it gets, the simpler my ask becomes. I am ready to carry a match, start to finish.
Name the test, and I will take it.
I will not make a threat about someone's health.
Let me take the plan in stages. I want to be the one calling the shots in a match.
I want a chance before people decide what I am. If you think I have not improved, come and test it.
My demand shrinks to one point when it heats up.
Give me a match and I will show you I can run it.
I have watched others lead matches, and now I want my turn. I will compete hard but I will not try to hurt you.
I would rather be slow and right. My next goal is to lead a match on my own terms.
My aim is a clean contest, not a grudge with consequences.
I narrow everything down to one demand under strain. Test me properly, and I will test you back.
If someone dismisses my progress, I will answer it in the ring. I would rather be slow and right.
